intended_object: The finite (generically simple) group of Lie type B_n(q) ≅ Ω_{2n+1}(q)/Z, built by the Steinberg recipe [H,H]/Z([H,H]), where H is the group of Frobenius-fixed points of the type-B_n group over the algebraic closure of F_p. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and FixedPointCandidate.
explanation: `Group` unfolds to `FixedPointCandidate d.steinberg`, which is `DerivedCentralQuotient (fixedSubgroup d.steinberg)`, and that is `commutator H ⧸ center (commutator H)`. This is exactly [H,H]/Z([H,H]). The Steinberg map is the q-power Frobenius, raising every matrix entry to the q-th power, on the points over the algebraic closure of the full-weight type-B spin carrier. That is correct because the family is untwisted, and its fixed points are the carrier's points over F_q (`mem_fixedSubgroup_steinberg_iff`, `pointsMulEquivFixedSubgroupFrobenius`). The rank offset r−1 of the carrier is checked by `carrierRank_add_one`, using rank ≥ 2. The carrier is not proved to be the pinned simply connected group scheme, and the docstring says so explicitly. This does not affect the result: for any group of type B_n, the derived subgroup of the F_q-points modulo its centre is B_n(q) whatever the isogeny type, and the carrier's simple-root subgroups sit at the type-B simple roots. The definition names a specific family, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no finite groups of Lie type or Steinberg fixed-point quotients.
